xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4859: Open in editor on an SSH-host machine targets ssh-remote+127.0.0.1 (the local forward)

plan.title: Open in editor on an SSH-host machine targets ssh-remote+127.0.0.1 (the local forward)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: For a machine added as an SSH host (PAN-4404), the link's only ssh route is the local port forward tcp://127.0.0.1:<localPort>. sshHostFor in src/dashboard/server/services/open-remote.ts takes the first ssh route's hostname, so Open in editor launches `code --remote ssh-remote+127.0.0.1 <cwd>`, which opens the viewing machine's own SSH server instead of the SSH host.
narratives.Proposal: The route handler looks up the SSH machine record by link id (getSshMachineByLinkId) and passes its destination to resolveRemoteEditorLaunch. A new parseSshDestination in src/lib/anywhere/ssh/target.ts splits the destination into user/host/port; a new sshRemoteAuthority in open-remote.ts renders the Remote-SSH authority: plain [user@]host, or lowercase hex of JSON {hostName,user,port} when a port, an IPv6 host or an uppercase letter is present. Host order: SSH record destination, then the tailnet /ws/link route, then any tailnet route, else 409 no-ssh-host. ssh routes are local forwards and are never used as an editor host. configuration/linked-machines.mdx states the new rule.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to how SSH machines are added, forwarded or stored; no new fields in ssh-machines.json.
- No per-editor authority encodings, and no Cursor/Windsurf remote support.
- No change to the PanOpenInPicker UI; the long hex commandLine echo is accepted.
- No destination field added to the open-in-editor response.
- No change to tailnet-route behavior or to the editor-unsupported / no-cwd responses.
- No fallback that ever returns an ssh route's hostname (that is the bug).
- No change to docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md.

autoDecisions.summary: Host order is SSH machine record destination, then tailnet /ws/link route, then any tailnet route, else no-ssh-host; ssh routes are never a host source.
autoDecisions.rationale: kind 'ssh' is assigned only by ssh-machine-service.ts:301 and always points at tcp://127.0.0.1:<localPort>; the record's destination is the address the dashboard's own ssh client already reaches.

autoDecisions.summary: Authority encoding: plain [user@]host unless a port, an IPv6 host or an uppercase letter is present, then hex JSON {hostName,user,port}.
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified against jeanp413/open-remote-ssh (VSCodium) sshDestination.ts and the installed anysphere.remote-ssh parser: both decode hex JSON with those keys; the plain parser splits the port on the last ':' (breaks IPv6) and vscode.uri lowercases the authority. Plain stays for the common case so existing tailnet output is unchanged.

autoDecisions.summary: The destination parser lives in src/lib/anywhere/ssh/target.ts and validates first.
autoDecisions.rationale: That module's header makes it the single owner of every destination string; reusing validateSshDestination keeps one grammar.

autoDecisions.summary: The no-ssh-host 409 message becomes '<label> has no SSH host (not an SSH machine and no tailnet route)'.
autoDecisions.rationale: The old text mentions an ssh route, which no longer counts.

autoDecisions.summary: Microsoft's proprietary Remote-SSH is not installed, so the hex form is unit-tested only; if a later live check shows it rejects hex, file a follow-up rather than adding per-editor encodings.
autoDecisions.rationale: Two Remote-SSH implementations share the hex shape; the issue itself named the hex-encoded JSON authority as the expected form for ports.

items.title: Add parseSshDestination to src/lib/anywhere/ssh/target.ts

expected_outputs: target.test.ts passes including the new parseSshDestination describe block

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. Export interface ParsedSshDestination { user?: string; host: string; port?: number } and function parseSshDestination(input) right after isValidSshDestination. It calls validateSshDestination first (so it throws SshMachineError 'bad-destination' for rejected input), strips 'ssh://', splits the user on the first '@', strips IPv6 brackets and reads an optional ':port'. Omit absent keys from the result. Add a describe('parseSshDestination') block with every row of the PRD WI-1 table.

items.title: Given 'ssh://root@build-box:2222', parseSshDestination returns { user: 'root', host: 'build-box', port: 2222 }; given 'build-box' it returns { host: 'build-box' } with no user or port keys
Given 'ssh://me@[fd00::5]:2200', it returns { user: 'me', host: 'fd00::5', port: 2200 }; given '[fd00::5]' it returns { host: 'fd00::5' }
Given 'build-box:2222', '-oProxyCommand=x' or '', it throws an SshMachineError whose code is 'bad-destination'
Add sshRemoteAuthority (plain or hex JSON) to open-remote.ts

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2 / D-2. export function sshRemoteAuthority(destination: string): string using parseSshDestination. Return plain `${user}@${host}` (or host) unless port is set, host contains ':', or the plain string matches /[A-Z]/; then return Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ hostName: host, user, port }), 'utf8').toString('hex') (key order hostName, user, port; undefined keys omitted by JSON.stringify; port is a number). Add tests for every row of the PRD WI-2 table, with the exact hex strings.

items.title: sshRemoteAuthority returns 'root@build-box' for 'root@build-box' and for 'ssh://root@build-box', and 'build-box' for 'build-box'
sshRemoteAuthority('[::1]') returns '7b22686f73744e616d65223a223a3a31227d' and 'Admin@build-box' returns hex that decodes to { hostName: 'build-box', user: 'Admin' }
resolveRemoteEditorLaunch uses the SSH destination and never an ssh route's host

expected_outputs: open-remote.test.ts passes, including the issue reproduction case

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3 / D-1. Delete the ssh-route branch from sshHostFor (keep the tailnet logic unchanged). Add optional `sshDestination?: string | null` to resolveRemoteEditorLaunch's input; authority = destinationAuthority(sshDestination) ?? sshHostFor(link), where destinationAuthority wraps sshRemoteAuthority in try/catch and returns null on a throw. Rewrite the module header (lines 1-10): record destination first, then tailnet /ws/link, then any tailnet route; ssh routes are local forwards and never used; one sentence on the plain/hex rule. In the tests, replace the assertion that expects 'desk-ssh' from an ssh route with the same routes expecting 'desk.tail1234.ts.net', and add the PRD WI-3 cases (issue repro, destination wins over tailnet, ssh+tailnet without destination, bad destination falls back). Verify the second clause of ac4 by reading the diff, not with a test that reads source files (source-reading tests fail lint).

items.title: Given routes [ssh tcp://127.0.0.1:40123] and no sshDestination, resolveRemoteEditorLaunch returns { error: 'no-ssh-host' }

Given the same routes and sshDestination 'ssh://root@build-box:2222', it returns args ['--remote', 'ssh-remote+7b22686f73744e616d65223a226275696c642d626f78222c2275736572223a22726f6f74222c22706f7274223a323232327d', '/home/root/project']

Given sshDestination 'root@build-box' and a tailnet /ws/link route, it returns 'ssh-remote+root@build-box'; given sshDestination '-bad' and that tailnet route, it falls back to 'ssh-remote+desk.tail1234.ts.net'
sshHostFor on routes [tailnet wss://desk.tail1234.ts.net/ws/link, ssh tcp://desk-ssh:22] returns 'desk.tail1234.ts.net', and open-remote.ts contains no code that reads an ssh-kind route's hostname
Open-in-editor route looks up the SSH machine record by link id

expected_outputs: open-remote.test.ts passes including the SSH-linked handler cases
typecheck and lint complete without errors

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4 / D-5. Add `getSshMachine: (linkId: string) => Promise<SshMachineRecord | null>` to LinkedOpenDeps with default getSshMachineByLinkId from '../../../lib/anywhere/ssh/machine-store.js'. After the no-cwd check, `const sshMachine = await deps.getSshMachine(link.id)` and pass `sshDestination: sshMachine?.destination ?? null`. Change the no-ssh-host message to `${link.label} has no SSH host (not an SSH machine and no tailnet route)`. Existing handler tests pass `getSshMachine: async () => null`. Add the PRD WI-4 handler tests.

items.title: Given an SSH-linked machine (routes [ssh tcp://127.0.0.1:40123], getSshMachine returns destination 'ssh://root@build-box:2222'), handleLinkedOpenInEditor returns 200, launches code with the WI-2 hex authority, and its commandLine contains no '127.0.0.1'
When handleLinkedOpenInEditor runs for @desk/conv-x, it calls getSshMachine with the link id "link-desk"

Given getSshMachine returns null and only the ssh route exists, it returns 409 with code 'no-ssh-host' and error 'desk has no SSH host (not an SSH machine and no tailnet route)', and launch is not called
Document the SSH machine host rule in configuration/linked-machines.mdx

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5. In configuration/linked-machines.mdx, section '## Open in editor', replace the sentence "The host is the link's `ssh` route when there is one, else its Tailscale (`tailnet`) route's host name; a link with neither cannot do this (`no-ssh-host`)." with: for a machine added as an SSH machine the host is the destination you added it with (for example `ssh-remote+root@build-box`), never the local port forward; otherwise the link's Tailscale (`tailnet`) host name; a link with neither cannot do this (`no-ssh-host`); a destination with a port, an IPv6 address or an uppercase letter is passed in Remote-SSH's encoded form (hex of {"hostName","user","port"}), so the command line shows a long hex string. Include the literal phrase 'destination you added it with'.
